# Build Your Coding Agent with Google ADK

## Welcome

A coding agent isn't magic. It's a model, a few tools and a loop. In this tutorial you build one
with Google's **Agent Development Kit (ADK)**, until it can take a small Python project with
failing tests and turn them green on its own.

![The agent loop](https://omarcevi.dev/workshops/coding-agent-workshop/diagrams/agent-loop.svg)

[Open the diagram full size](https://omarcevi.dev/workshops/coding-agent-workshop/diagrams/agent-loop.svg)

| Step | You add | Then the agent can |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | A model and an instruction | talk about code, but not see yours |
| 2 | `list_files`, `read_file`, `write_file` | look at the project and change it |
| 3 | `run_command` | run the tests and fix until they pass |
| 4 | A path check and approvals | only touch the project, and only with your OK |

You build the agent in <walkthrough-editor-open-file filePath="agents/my_agent/agent.py">agents/my_agent/agent.py</walkthrough-editor-open-file>. In each step you paste the next version of the
file over it. The finished version of every step is also in the `agents/` folder.

You need a free Gemini API key. You don't need a Google Cloud project or billing. The guide has
the full explanations: [omarcevi.dev/workshops/coding-agent-workshop](https://omarcevi.dev/workshops/coding-agent-workshop/).

<walkthrough-tutorial-duration duration="60"></walkthrough-tutorial-duration>

## Set up

1. Install uv, the Python package manager. If Cloud Shell already has uv, the script only shows
   its version:
   ```bash
   source scripts/install_uv.sh
   ```
2. Install the Python packages (about 1 minute):
   ```bash
   uv sync
   ```
3. Get a free Gemini API key at [aistudio.google.com/apikey](https://aistudio.google.com/apikey).
4. Save the key. The script asks for the key. The key does not show on the screen when you paste
   it:
   ```bash
   uv run python scripts/set_key.py
   ```
   The script saves the key in <walkthrough-editor-open-file filePath=".env">.env</walkthrough-editor-open-file>.
5. Create the practice project. It copies <walkthrough-editor-open-file filePath="demo_project/cart.py">a small shopping cart</walkthrough-editor-open-file>
   with two bugs into `workspace/`, the only folder the agent works in:
   ```bash
   uv run reset_workspace.py
   ```
6. Check everything, including one call to Gemini:
   ```bash
   uv run check_setup.py
   ```

✅ **Check:** every line says `OK`, and the last one shows Gemini's answer.

## Step 1 · An agent with no tools

An ADK agent is a model plus an instruction. `adk web` looks for a variable called `root_agent`
in `agent.py` and gives you a chat window for it. Open <walkthrough-editor-open-file filePath="agents/my_agent/agent.py">agents/my_agent/agent.py</walkthrough-editor-open-file>: it already holds
the whole of step 1.

### Run it

Start the ADK dev UI in the terminal:

```bash
uv run adk web --reload_agents --port 8080 --allow_origins https://8080-$WEB_HOST agents
```

`adk web` loads each folder in `agents/` as an app. With `--reload_agents`, it loads a file again
when you save it. With `--allow_origins`, the Web Preview page can connect to the dev UI.

1. Click <walkthrough-web-preview-icon></walkthrough-web-preview-icon> **Web preview**. Then click
   **Preview on port 8080**. The dev UI opens in a new tab.
2. Click **+** in the terminal to open a second tab. Use it for all other commands. The dev UI
   keeps running in the first tab.

In the dev UI, select `my_agent` in **Select an app** at the top. Then send:

```text
The tests in my project are failing. Can you fix them?
```

✅ **Check:** it can't see your files. It asks you to paste the code, or it guesses a generic fix.

More about this step: [Step 1 · An agent with no tools](https://omarcevi.dev/workshops/coding-agent-workshop/step-1/).

## Step 2 · Give it hands

Tools in ADK are plain Python functions. ADK reads each function's name, type hints and
docstring, and sends them to the model as a tool definition. The model never runs your code: it
asks for a call, ADK runs the function, and the result goes back to the model.

New in this version: `list_files`, `read_file` and `write_file`, the `WORKSPACE` folder they work
in, and `tools=[...]` on the agent.

### Paste the new version

**Copy the code.** Click the copy button at the top right of the code below. It's the whole
file, with the new parts explained in its comments.

```python
"""Step 2: give the agent hands. Tools to look at and change files.

ADK turns each plain Python function below into a tool. The model sees only
the function's name, its type hints and its docstring, so the docstring is
written for the model, not for you.

Try: "What's in my project, and what does cart.py do?"
     "Create hello.py that prints a greeting."
"""

from pathlib import Path

from google.adk.agents import Agent

# The folder the agent works in. Recreate it with: uv run reset_workspace.py
WORKSPACE = Path(__file__).resolve().parents[2] / "workspace"
SKIP = {"__pycache__", ".pytest_cache"}


def list_files() -> dict:
    """Lists every file in the project, as paths relative to the project root."""
    files = [
        str(p.relative_to(WORKSPACE))
        for p in sorted(WORKSPACE.rglob("*"))
        if p.is_file() and not SKIP & set(p.parts)
    ]
    return {"files": files}


# Tools return errors instead of raising them. ADK re-raises a tool's
# exception and ends the run, but an error the model can read is one it can
# recover from (e.g. "no such file", then it lists files and tries again).


def read_file(path: str) -> dict:
    """Reads a text file from the project.

    Args:
        path: File path relative to the project root, e.g. "cart.py".
    """
    try:
        return {"content": (WORKSPACE / path).read_text()}
    except Exception as e:
        return {"error": str(e)}


def write_file(path: str, content: str) -> dict:
    """Creates a file, or replaces an existing file's contents.

    Args:
        path: File path relative to the project root, e.g. "cart.py".
        content: The complete new contents of the file.
    """
    try:
        file = WORKSPACE / path
        file.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
        file.write_text(content)
        return {"status": "ok", "path": path}
    except Exception as e:
        return {"error": str(e)}


root_agent = Agent(
    name="coding_agent",
    model="gemini-3.8-flash",
    instruction=(
        "You are a coding agent working on a small Python project. "
        "Look before you answer: list the files, then read the ones that matter. "
        "When you change a file, write its complete new contents. "
        "Finish with a short summary of what you did."
    ),
    tools=[list_files, read_file, write_file],
)
```

**Paste and save.** Click <walkthrough-editor-open-file filePath="agents/my_agent/agent.py">agents/my_agent/agent.py</walkthrough-editor-open-file> to open it. Press Ctrl+A (⌘A on a Mac) to
select everything, Ctrl+V (⌘V) to paste over it, then Ctrl+S (⌘S) to save.

The same file is in <walkthrough-editor-open-file filePath="agents/step2_files/agent.py">agents/step2_files/agent.py</walkthrough-editor-open-file>. If you'd rather read than
paste, select `step2_files` in the dev UI instead of `my_agent`.

### Run it

The dev UI from step 1 keeps running in the first terminal tab, and it loads your file again when
you save. If it stopped, run this again in the first tab:

```bash
uv run adk web --reload_agents --port 8080 --allow_origins https://8080-$WEB_HOST agents
```

Then send these, one at a time:

```text
What's in my project, and what does cart.py do?
```

```text
Create hello.py that prints a greeting.
```

✅ **Check:** the chat shows calls to `list_files` and `read_file`. Click one to see what the
model asked for and what came back. <walkthrough-editor-open-file filePath="workspace/hello.py">workspace/hello.py</walkthrough-editor-open-file> now exists.

More about this step: [Step 2 · Give it hands](https://omarcevi.dev/workshops/coding-agent-workshop/step-2/).

## Step 3 · Close the loop

With file tools alone, the agent edits code and hopes. Give it a way to run commands and it can
check its own work: run the tests, read the failures, fix, and run them again.

New in this version: `run_command`, and one sentence in the instruction: run the tests after every
change, and keep fixing until they pass.

### Paste the new version

**Copy the code.** Click the copy button at the top right of the code below. It's the whole
file, with the new parts explained in its comments.

```python
"""Step 3: close the loop. The agent can run code and see what happened.

With file tools alone the agent edits code and hopes. With run_command it
can run the tests, read the failures, fix, and run them again. That loop is
what makes it a coding agent. ADK runs the loop for you: call the model, run
the tool it asks for, send back the result, repeat until it answers in text.

Try: "The tests are failing. Fix them."
"""

import subprocess
from pathlib import Path

from google.adk.agents import Agent

# The folder the agent works in. Recreate it with: uv run reset_workspace.py
WORKSPACE = Path(__file__).resolve().parents[2] / "workspace"
SKIP = {"__pycache__", ".pytest_cache"}


def list_files() -> dict:
    """Lists every file in the project, as paths relative to the project root."""
    files = [
        str(p.relative_to(WORKSPACE))
        for p in sorted(WORKSPACE.rglob("*"))
        if p.is_file() and not SKIP & set(p.parts)
    ]
    return {"files": files}


def read_file(path: str) -> dict:
    """Reads a text file from the project.

    Args:
        path: File path relative to the project root, e.g. "cart.py".
    """
    try:
        return {"content": (WORKSPACE / path).read_text()}
    except Exception as e:
        return {"error": str(e)}


def write_file(path: str, content: str) -> dict:
    """Creates a file, or replaces an existing file's contents.

    Args:
        path: File path relative to the project root, e.g. "cart.py".
        content: The complete new contents of the file.
    """
    try:
        file = WORKSPACE / path
        file.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
        file.write_text(content)
        return {"status": "ok", "path": path}
    except Exception as e:
        return {"error": str(e)}


def run_command(command: str) -> dict:
    """Runs a shell command in the project folder and returns its output.
    Use it to run code and tests, e.g. "python -m pytest".

    Args:
        command: The shell command to run.
    """
    try:
        result = subprocess.run(
            command,
            shell=True,
            cwd=WORKSPACE,
            capture_output=True,
            text=True,
            timeout=30,  # a hung command must not freeze the agent
        )
    except subprocess.TimeoutExpired:
        return {"error": "Command timed out after 30 seconds."}
    return {
        "exit_code": result.returncode,
        # Keep the end of long output: that's where errors and test summaries are.
        "stdout": result.stdout[-4000:],
        "stderr": result.stderr[-4000:],
    }


root_agent = Agent(
    name="coding_agent",
    model="gemini-3.8-flash",
    instruction=(
        "You are a coding agent working on a small Python project. "
        "Look before you answer: list the files, then read the ones that matter. "
        "When you change a file, write its complete new contents. "
        "After every change, run the tests with `python -m pytest` and keep "
        "fixing until they all pass. "
        "Finish with a short summary of what you changed and the test result."
    ),
    tools=[list_files, read_file, write_file, run_command],
)
```

**Paste and save.** Click <walkthrough-editor-open-file filePath="agents/my_agent/agent.py">agents/my_agent/agent.py</walkthrough-editor-open-file> to open it. Press Ctrl+A (⌘A on a Mac) to
select everything, Ctrl+V (⌘V) to paste over it, then Ctrl+S (⌘S) to save.

The same file is in <walkthrough-editor-open-file filePath="agents/step3_run/agent.py">agents/step3_run/agent.py</walkthrough-editor-open-file>. If you'd rather read than
paste, select `step3_run` in the dev UI instead of `my_agent`.

### Run it

The dev UI from step 1 keeps running in the first terminal tab, and it loads your file again when
you save. If it stopped, run this again in the first tab:

```bash
uv run adk web --reload_agents --port 8080 --allow_origins https://8080-$WEB_HOST agents
```

In your second terminal tab, put the buggy project back:

```bash
uv run reset_workspace.py
```

Then send:

```text
The tests are failing. Fix them.
```

✅ **Check:** it runs `python -m pytest` (3 failed, 1 passed), reads the files, writes a fix and
runs the tests again (4 passed). It takes about 25 seconds. See the fix in
<walkthrough-editor-open-file filePath="workspace/cart.py">workspace/cart.py</walkthrough-editor-open-file>.

More about this step: [Step 3 · Close the loop](https://omarcevi.dev/workshops/coding-agent-workshop/step-3/).

## Step 4 · Add guardrails

Step 3 works, and that's the problem. Nothing stops it from reading `../.env`, where your key
lives, or running any command it likes.

New in this version: `_resolve`, which refuses any path outside the workspace, and
`FunctionTool(..., require_confirmation=True)` on `write_file` and `run_command`, so the dev UI asks
you before each one.

### Paste the new version

**Copy the code.** Click the copy button at the top right of the code below. It's the whole
file, with the new parts explained in its comments.

```python
"""Step 4: add guardrails before you let it loose on your laptop.

Step 3 works, but nothing stops the agent from reading ../.env or running
any shell command it likes. Two guardrails:

1. File tools refuse any path outside the workspace (see _resolve).
2. Writing files and running commands ask you first.
   `require_confirmation=True` pauses the run and `adk web` shows a card
   with the arguments: tick "Confirmed" and press Submit to allow it, or
   press Submit unticked to reject it.

Why confirm writes too? Approving "python -m pytest" approves whatever code
the tests load, and the agent could have just written a conftest.py.
Confirming every write means every line that runs is one you have seen.

These are guardrails, not a sandbox: an approved command can still do
anything you can. Real isolation needs a container or a VM.

Try: "Read ../pyproject.toml"          (refused: outside the workspace)
     "The tests are failing. Fix them." (approve the fix, then each test run)
"""

import subprocess
from pathlib import Path

from google.adk.agents import Agent
from google.adk.tools import FunctionTool

# The folder the agent works in. Recreate it with: uv run reset_workspace.py
WORKSPACE = (Path(__file__).resolve().parents[2] / "workspace").resolve()
SKIP = {"__pycache__", ".pytest_cache"}


def _resolve(path: str) -> Path:
    """Turns a project-relative path into a real path, refusing anything outside
    the workspace: "../.env", "/etc/passwd", or a symlink that points out."""
    file = (WORKSPACE / path).resolve()
    if not file.is_relative_to(WORKSPACE):
        raise PermissionError(f"{path!r} is outside the project folder.")
    return file


def list_files() -> dict:
    """Lists every file in the project, as paths relative to the project root."""
    files = [
        str(p.relative_to(WORKSPACE))
        for p in sorted(WORKSPACE.rglob("*"))
        if p.is_file() and not SKIP & set(p.parts)
    ]
    return {"files": files}


def read_file(path: str) -> dict:
    """Reads a text file from the project.

    Args:
        path: File path relative to the project root, e.g. "cart.py".
    """
    try:
        return {"content": _resolve(path).read_text()}
    except Exception as e:
        return {"error": str(e)}


def write_file(path: str, content: str) -> dict:
    """Creates a file, or replaces an existing file's contents.

    Args:
        path: File path relative to the project root, e.g. "cart.py".
        content: The complete new contents of the file.
    """
    try:
        file = _resolve(path)
        file.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
        file.write_text(content)
        return {"status": "ok", "path": path}
    except Exception as e:
        return {"error": str(e)}


def run_command(command: str) -> dict:
    """Runs a shell command in the project folder and returns its output.
    Use it to run code and tests, e.g. "python -m pytest".

    Args:
        command: The shell command to run.
    """
    try:
        result = subprocess.run(
            command,
            shell=True,
            cwd=WORKSPACE,
            capture_output=True,
            text=True,
            timeout=30,  # a hung command must not freeze the agent
        )
    except subprocess.TimeoutExpired:
        return {"error": "Command timed out after 30 seconds."}
    return {
        "exit_code": result.returncode,
        # Keep the end of long output: that's where errors and test summaries are.
        "stdout": result.stdout[-4000:],
        "stderr": result.stderr[-4000:],
    }


root_agent = Agent(
    name="coding_agent",
    model="gemini-3.8-flash",
    instruction=(
        "You are a coding agent working on a small Python project. "
        "Look before you answer: list the files, then read the ones that matter. "
        "When you change a file, write its complete new contents. "
        "After every change, run the tests with `python -m pytest` and keep "
        "fixing until they all pass. "
        "Only work inside the project folder. If the user rejects a tool call, "
        "do not retry it; explain what you wanted to do instead. "
        "Finish with a short summary of what you changed and the test result."
    ),
    tools=[
        list_files,
        read_file,
        # Wrapping a function in FunctionTool lets you configure it.
        FunctionTool(write_file, require_confirmation=True),
        FunctionTool(run_command, require_confirmation=True),
    ],
)
```

**Paste and save.** Click <walkthrough-editor-open-file filePath="agents/my_agent/agent.py">agents/my_agent/agent.py</walkthrough-editor-open-file> to open it. Press Ctrl+A (⌘A on a Mac) to
select everything, Ctrl+V (⌘V) to paste over it, then Ctrl+S (⌘S) to save.

The same file is in <walkthrough-editor-open-file filePath="agents/step4_safe/agent.py">agents/step4_safe/agent.py</walkthrough-editor-open-file>. If you'd rather read than
paste, select `step4_safe` in the dev UI instead of `my_agent`.

### Run it

The dev UI from step 1 keeps running in the first terminal tab, and it loads your file again when
you save. If it stopped, run this again in the first tab:

```bash
uv run adk web --reload_agents --port 8080 --allow_origins https://8080-$WEB_HOST agents
```

Try to get out of the folder:

```text
Read ../pyproject.toml
```

✅ **Check:** it's refused: the path is outside the project folder.

Now reset the project in your second terminal tab, and ask it to fix the tests again:

```bash
uv run reset_workspace.py
```

```text
The tests are failing. Fix them.
```

Each write and each command shows a card with its arguments. Tick **Confirmed** and click
**Submit** to allow it. To reject it, click **Submit** without ticking. If it asks for something
you didn't ask for, like `git diff`, reject it and watch what it does.

✅ **Check:** you approve a test run, the fix and a second test run, and the tests pass.

More about this step: [Step 4 · Add guardrails](https://omarcevi.dev/workshops/coding-agent-workshop/step-4/).

## Well done

You built a coding agent: a model, four tools, a loop that ADK runs for you, and guardrails that
keep you in charge.
